shared: The Tyre is a medium-weight aerospace fighter developed by Clan Steel Viper in 2907, conceived as a homegrown successor to the Corsair class fighter that had nearly vanished among the Clans' ancestors during the long journey from the Inner Sphere. After years of iterative development and numerous proposed enhancements, Viper designers settled on a design that deliberately traded maximum speed for resilience and concentrated firepower, producing a craft ideally suited to the DropShip escort role the Clan urgently needed to fill. Economical to operate and straightforward to maintain by Clan standards, the Tyre found a ready home not only in Steel Viper aerospace forces but across much of the Clan homeworld complex. While newer OmniFighters eventually displaced it from front-line duty among wealthier Clans, the Tyre remained a fixture of second-line forces throughout the Clan universe, valued for dependability and sustained combat effectiveness against both aerospace and ground targets.

Built around economy and durability rather than raw performance, the Tyre mounts a standard fusion powerplant that limits it to a top acceleration of four Gs, average by the standards of heavier craft but deliberately matched to the pace of the DropShips it was designed to escort. The design philosophy treats this modest speed as a feature, keeping the fighter close to its assigned convoy rather than being lured away by enemy interceptors seeking to draw off the screen.

Seven and a half tons of Formula TSF Standard armor protects the airframe, with additional mass concentrated in the nose and forward fuselage to survive frontal engagement. The primary armament pairs a Type 9-A Ultra autocannon with seven Series AP7 medium pulse lasers, a combination that emphasizes concentrated close-range firepower over standoff reach. All weapons may be fired simultaneously without overtaxing the heat sinks, making the Tyre an exceptionally reliable strafing platform against surface targets and an unforgiving opponent at close quarters.

The trade-off is a significant lack of reach, and opposing fighters who maintain their distance hold a clear tactical advantage. Heat dissipation is matched tightly to the weapons load with little surplus, leaving pilots minimal margin during extended engagements. Both weaknesses are well-understood among Clan aerospace pilots, and the Tyre's tactical reputation reflects a design that punishes the enemy hardest when it can close the range.

The Tyre traces its lineage back to the Corsair, the capable medium fighter that served as a backbone of Star League aerospace forces before Operation Exodus. The Corsair had seen heavy attrition during the liberation of Terra and the years of conflict that followed, and by the time Kerensky's forces departed the Inner Sphere the design was already declining in availability. The journey across the void further reduced their numbers, and when the Clans were formed from the survivors of the Exodus fleet, functioning Corsairs had become scarce, leaving the warrior caste dependent on whatever craft had survived the long passage.

Clan Steel Viper aerospace engineers undertook a deliberate program to fill this gap, studying the Corsair's operational strengths and the particular demands of the nascent Clan military. Numerous design proposals were advanced, tested, and revised over the course of several years. Performance characteristics were adjusted, weapons configurations evaluated, and structural details refined through the iterative process common to early Clan engineering efforts. Viper designers finally declared success in 2907, fielding what they named the Tyre. The new fighter quickly became the foundation of the Clan's aerospace fleet, serving primarily as the premier escort for DropShips moving through potentially hostile space.

Through the Trials and trading that shaped Clan interactions during the homeworld period, the Tyre spread widely among the other Clans. Production facilities were established on New Kent, Albion, Bearclaw, Babylon, Homer, Roche, and York, giving nearly every Clan access to domestically produced examples at various points during the early centuries. As OmniFighters were developed and proliferated among the wealthier Clans during the later Golden Century and into the Clan Invasion era, the Tyre was progressively shifted to second-line assignments. Clans historically short on resources for OmniFighters continued using Tyres in front-line roles, and all Clans maintained some quantity in their reserve aerospace forces.

The Steel Vipers maintained the most concentrated production at their New Kent orbital facility, which became the definitive source of later production runs as other homeworld facilities scaled back or ceased operations. The Vipers' eventual Annihilation following the Wars of Reaving brought New Kent production to an end, but the design found an unexpected second life in the Inner Sphere when Janesek Industries on Orestes began producing modified variants under Ghost Bear occupation during the Dark Age, later continuing under Republic Dominion sponsorship and extending the Tyre's service well into the ilClan era.

The Vandal is a thirty-ton Clan OmniFighter developed in 2941 by Clan Ice Hellion, conceived from the outset as a high-speed scout and pursuit craft rather than a front-line combatant. Its exceptional agility distinguishes it from heavier fighters of comparable cost, though its limited weapons payload means most Clan commanders assign it to reconnaissance and rear-echelon screening duties rather than direct combat. Every Clan maintains Vandals for fast scouting work, and the design has spread widely through salvage and Trials since its introduction. The years following the Great Refusal gave the craft renewed relevance, particularly among the home Clans, who recognized it as an economical platform for power projection. Clan Hell's Horses became its most committed later-era patron, investing in new production capacity to sustain the type through the Dark Age.

The Vandal's defining characteristic is its exceptional thrust-to-weight ratio, which makes it among the most agile fighters in the Clan inventory. Its 360 XL engine provides the acceleration needed to disengage from heavier interceptors that cannot match its pace. The Tokasha Foundry Series 9 ferro-aluminum armor offers adequate protection for a craft of its weight, though pilots who linger in a defensive engagement against dedicated combat fighters do so at considerable risk. The primary configuration mounts an active probe in place of heavier offensive weapons, making the craft an effective sensor platform when operating as the eyes of a Trinary or Cluster. An additional ton of fuel in this configuration gives it superior mission endurance compared to the alternate configurations. The pair of nose-mounted small lasers provides minimal self-defense capability, though aggressive pilots have been known to use them against soft ground targets during reconnaissance passes.

The Vandal's OmniFighter pod system allows rapid reconfiguration between its roles. The tradeoff in each alternate configuration is straightforward: sensor equipment gives way to weapons as the mission emphasis shifts from reconnaissance to attack. None of the configurations are optimized for stand-up dogfighting against comparable Clan fighters; the Vandal's strengths lie in speed, endurance, and surprise rather than raw firepower.

Clan Ice Hellion developed the Vandal in 2941 at the Yoma Aerospace Plant on Babylon, in the Kerensky Cluster. The Ice Hellions' preference for swift, aggressive raiding tactics made a fast light fighter a natural fit for their doctrine, and the design spread to other Clans through Trials and the normal exchange of genetic and technical resources. Within a generation, the Vandal had found a place in virtually every Clan touman, typically filling the scouting and screening roles that larger fighters could not perform as economically.

The Vandal's reputation as a freeborn fighter's craft developed early in its service history. Clan commanders discovered that the threat of assignment to Vandal duty was sufficient to keep undisciplined freeborn pilots in line, and this association suppressed tactical innovation with the design for decades. Few Bloodnamed warriors cared to be seen developing doctrine for what their peers regarded as a punishment posting. This cultural stigma meant the Vandal rarely received the doctrinal attention or logistical priority that designs of its quality deserved.

The Clan Invasion brought Vandals to the Inner Sphere, where they found employment in reconnaissance and pursuit roles that complemented the heavier OmniFighters dominating Clan aerospace assets. Their ability to outrun Inner Sphere conventional fighters gave them genuine tactical value, and several Clans quietly expanded their Vandal inventories without public acknowledgment. The years following the Great Refusal accelerated this reassessment as the home Clans began competing more aggressively for resources and prestige within the Kerensky Cluster.

Clan Hell's Horses emerged as the most vocal advocate for the Vandal's combat capabilities, incorporating the craft into fast-attack operations and forward screening duties that leveraged its speed advantages. The Wars of Reaving and the collapse of Clan Ice Hellion transferred the Babylon production facility to Cloud Cobra control, which continued production through the Dark Age. Clan Hell's Horses subsequently established a second production line at the Csesztreg Industriplex Delta, coming online during the Dark Age to supply their expanding toumans independently. By the ilClan era, the Vandal had largely shed its freeborn stigma and earned genuine respect as a capable scout and pursuit platform.

text.overview: Rashpur-Owens Incorporated, the Capellan aerospace firm best known for its assault DropShip lines, entered the fighter market in the 3070s as a deliberate strategy to diversify revenue and reduce reliance on spacecraft contracts alone. The company had clawed its way back from near-insolvency several times during the Succession Wars, and while strong DropShip sales carried it through the Jihad, leadership recognized the post-war environment as an opportunity to expand into a new product category. Design work proceeded with greater difficulty than anticipated, with engineering delays and failed subcomponent negotiations extending the timeline well beyond initial projections. The Magistracy of Canopus ultimately secured co-production rights, and the design entered service in 3081 as the MNG-8L, named the Měngqín. Despite a troubled development record, the aircraft found a receptive audience in the Capellan Confederation Armed Forces, the Magistracy Air Force, and mercenary commands operating across the former Inner Sphere.
text.capabilities:
The Měngqín is built around a mixed-range weapons array rather than a single dominant engagement envelope. Its nose mounts a pair of Ceres Arms Crusher plasma rifles and a Sian/Ceres Cougar SRM-6 rack, delivering concentrated short-to-medium firepower that can burn through armor and generate dangerous heat in enemy units simultaneously. Each wing carries an additional Sian/Ceres Cougar SRM-6, two Ceres Arms ER medium lasers, and a Delta Dart LRM-15, allowing the fighter to engage effectively at all ranges. Two rear-facing Diverse Optics Type 2 ER medium lasers and a Magna 200p small pulse laser cover the aft arc, discouraging pursuit. The Ceres MaserCom B-33 communications suite and Brightstar Model III targeting and tracking system support coordinated multi-range engagements.

The design has well-documented limitations. A full alpha strike exceeds the capacity of its seventeen double heat sinks by a meaningful margin, and committing to that level of fire risks a forced reactor shutdown. The plasma rifle, SRM, and LRM ammunition reserves barely meet the minimum standard expected for a fighter of this weight class, and pilots who engage aggressively without managing expenditure will exhaust their ammunition before the engagement concludes. The 14.5 tons of Detroit Ferro-Aluminum Special armor and the standard Pitban 285 fusion engine provide solid protection and adequate endurance within those constraints, and the cost-effective design philosophy that produced these trade-offs also kept the unit price within reach of the CCAF's procurement budget.
text.deployment:
The MNG-8L is the production-standard Měngqín and the design that emerged from Rashpur-Owens Incorporated's development program. Rashpur-Owens holds an exclusive supply contract with the Capellan Confederation Armed Forces, where the fighter has been well received across most CCAF commands. A notable number of the type have been observed along the borders of Confederation Prefectures V and VI, though analysts attribute this concentration to standard defensive deployments rather than any directed buildup.

In the Periphery, Detroit Consolidated Aerospace distributes the MNG-8L throughout Magistracy space, with initial production runs going to the Canopian Fusiliers and subsequent deliveries sold out through 3087. Detroit also exports the design to the broader Inner Sphere mercenary market via distribution networks operating across the former Capellan Confederation, the Republic of the Sphere, the former Free Worlds League, and Federated Suns territories. No variants have been produced to date.
text.battleHistory:
As military operations wound down following the Coalition's final campaigns against the Word of Blake, Rashpur-Owens Incorporated shifted its focus from wartime DropShip production to the uncertainty of a peacetime market. Having survived near-insolvency multiple times during the Succession Wars and re-established firm financial footing through DropShip sales booked through 3082, company leadership recognized that dependence on a single product category left the firm exposed. The decision to enter aerospace fighter production followed naturally from this analysis, though the assumption that DropShip manufacturing experience would translate cleanly to fighter design proved mistaken almost immediately.

Design requirements and functional specifications took six months longer to finalize than projected. Contract negotiations with Ceres Arms over the primary weapons package became so protracted that the deal appeared likely to collapse entirely, and when it was finally concluded, an earlier backup arrangement for alternative ER medium laser suppliers had already been executed. Rather than void that second contract, Rashpur-Owens incorporated components from both agreements, resulting in two different ER medium laser variants in the finished airframe. The last major hurdle was resolved in 3078, and prototype construction began on Capella shortly after.

Rashpur-Owens marketed the new fighter to buyers in the Confederation, the Magistracy, and the Taurian Concordat. The Taurians declined to evaluate it. The Magistracy required months of negotiation before agreeing to terms, and then only on the condition that the design also be licensed for production at Detroit Consolidated Aerospace. Production commenced in 3081, and internal Rashpur-Owens projections indicated the company would not recover its development investment until after the last unit of the initial 3088 production run was delivered. Despite this, the Capellan Confederation Armed Forces adopted the Měngqín enthusiastically, and Detroit began distributing the type to Magistracy commands and the broader mercenary market in the years that followed.

text.deployment: Designated for aerospace superiority and ground attack roles, the A configuration builds around an extended-range PPC paired with twin plasma rifles, a combination capable of stripping armor from the heaviest opponents while simultaneously degrading enemy heat management systems. Three tons of plasma rifle ammunition provides reasonable endurance. Eight additional double heat sinks work to contain the substantial waste heat generated by this loadout, though pilots are trained to manage firing sequences carefully to avoid thermal overload. The A configuration has seen use by LCAF strike units and Clan Wolf-in-Exile elements assigned to deep interdiction and anti-armor missions.

Reflecting the Hellcat's energy-intensive combat philosophy, the C configuration relies entirely on directed-energy weapons. Extended-range lasers of multiple scales in the nose are complemented by a large pulse laser for precision fire, with additional extended-range medium lasers covering the wings and aft arc. Even with seven additional double heat sinks, pilots must rely on volley fire to manage thermal buildup during sustained engagement. The C configuration is favored by units prioritizing combat endurance over peak burst output, particularly in extended aerospace denial operations where ammunition resupply is uncertain.

The A configuration sacrifices range for close-engagement concentration. The nose and each wing pair a medium pulse laser with an SRM-6 equipped with Artemis IV fire control, creating nine weapon systems in overlapping short-range fields of fire. Three tons of SRM ammunition provide solid battlefield endurance for extended engagements. Pilots favored this configuration for defensive screening duties and aggressive intercept missions, where closing quickly and overwhelming targets with massed short-range fire made the Ogotai's atmospheric handling problems irrelevant in the vacuum of space combat.
text.battleHistory:
The Ogotai entered service in 2874 as one of the earliest dedicated OmniFighter designs produced within Clan society, manufactured at DS Aero Assembly Site Alpha on Babylon by what was then still Clan Sea Fox. The design represented an ambitious early attempt to apply OmniPod technology to aerospace platforms, though the engineering difficulties that would define the first generation of Clan OmniFighters were quickly apparent. Atmospheric handling deficiencies relegated the Ogotai away from the close-air support assignments its designers intended, pushing it toward orbital interdiction and escort roles where those weaknesses were less damaging.

The Ogotai's capabilities in space combat were demonstrated in a well-documented engagement during the early Succession Wars era, when the Sea Foxes' Lambda Spina Galaxy stationed a full Star aboard the Aegis-class cruiser CSF Bloodlust. During a patrol in the Vinton system, the Star encountered a Clan Smoke Jaguar contingent that had arrived via pirate point and demanded safcon to the surface. When the request was refused and Jaguar DropShips and fighters launched in response, the Ogotai pilots used disciplined fire and careful timing to engage the assault, bidding away weapons in proper zellbrigen fashion while exploiting heat management advantages. A bold Jaguar Point of OmniFighters pursued the Sea Fox pilots all the way into the upper atmosphere in a dramatic maneuver, forcing an emergency landing far outside the designated Trial site. Both Jaguar pilots lost control in Vinton's lower atmosphere and crashed fatally into the planet's oceans. Enough Jaguar DropShips had been destroyed during the planetfall sequence that the assault commander lacked the forces to secure the surface, handing the engagement to the Sea Foxes.

The Ogotai continued in active service through the later Golden Century, demonstrating consistent reliability in its space-superiority role, but steadily improving OmniFighter technology left the design behind. Replacement parts and weapon modules ceased manufacture in the early 2990s, and the Sea Foxes formally abandoned the production line in favor of more versatile and dependable airframes. By that time the Ogotai had influenced a successor design: Clan Wolf developed the Jagatai using many of the Ogotai's design philosophies, introducing the new medium OmniFighter in 3016. Individual Ogotais continued operating long after factory support ended, their longevity a sign of Clan maintenance skill. Some eventually passed into Dark Caste hands, their sustained operation a mystery given the complete absence of manufacturer support for parts and armament.

text.deployment: The B configuration shifts the Ogotai toward long-range fire support. Five ER small lasers in the nose provide close-defense coverage against fighters that close to short range, while two wing-mounted LRM-20 launchers with a combined four tons of ammunition deliver heavy bombardment capability at extended range. This loadout proved effective in fleet support operations and defensive patrols, allowing Ogotai pilots to engage DropShips and massed fighter screens from distance. The B's emphasis on range suited its operators' preference for space and orbital operations and minimized exposure to the atmospheric conditions the airframe handled poorly.

An ER medium laser covers the rear arc for defensive use against pursuing fighters. Four additional heat sinks, bringing the total to sixteen, allow sustained fire across the weapon mix. text.overview: The Oni is a medium aerospace fighter developed by Wakazashi Enterprises at their Chatham facility for the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery, representing the first new non-OmniFighter design fielded by the Combine following the Clan Invasion. Named for the demonic figures of Japanese folklore, the 55-ton craft was designed to address a gap left by years of prioritizing upgrades to existing airframes and the development of OmniFighter technology. The Oni emphasizes protection and concentrated medium-range firepower, trading some maneuverability for a heavier and more affordable power plant. The DCMS received the fighter with considerable enthusiasm, recognizing its durability and hitting power as assets well suited to the defensive and patrol roles increasingly demanded of Combine aerospace assets.
text.capabilities:
The Oni is built around a balanced weapons mix that emphasizes sustained volume of fire at medium range with dependable long-range backup. Its nose-mounted Shigunga MRM-30 delivers a withering weight of missiles capable of saturating targets at medium engagement distances, while a Diverse Optics Sunbeam ER small laser provides close-range support. Each wing carries a Diverse Optics Type 30X ER large laser, extending the fighter's effective reach and giving it genuine long-range strike capability. Two tons of missile ammunition provides adequate reloads for normal combat sorties.

The fighter mounts six tons of Chatham "Bakemono" ferro-aluminum armor, providing protection comparable to heavier designs and giving it the resilience to absorb significant punishment. Thirteen double heat sinks manage its thermal load effectively under most conditions. The standard Shinobi 275 fusion engine is less powerful than an extralight equivalent, reducing maneuverability, but lowering manufacturing costs and improving structural robustness. The Wakazashi V-On airframe supports this configuration with a solid, maintainable structure, while the Garret T22 communications suite and Neko Megane 6 targeting system round out the design's electronics. The fighter's limited endurance is its acknowledged weakness, restricting mission duration and range without resupply.
text.deployment: Introduced in 3066, the ON-1 is the baseline production model and became the mainstay of Combine aerospace wings from the late Civil War era onward. It serves primarily in planetary defense and escort roles, where its combination of armor and medium-range firepower suits the defensive posture adopted by the DCMS during the post-Invasion period. The ON-1 remained in continuous production at Chatham and achieved wide distribution across Combine aerospace commands throughout the Dark Age and into the ilClan era.
text.battleHistory:
The Oni's development was shaped by nearly a decade of competing priorities following the Clan Invasion. When Clan Smoke Jaguar overran the production site of the Sai, the Combine's promising next-generation fighter, Wakazashi Enterprises redirected its resources toward upgrading proven existing designs and supporting the development of the Tatsu OmniFighter. Aerospace fighter development was deprioritized as BattleMech modernization demanded the lion's share of Combine military-industrial output.

By the late 3050s, with the S-7 omni-conversion variant of the Sai established in service and the Tatsu program underway, Wakazashi finally had the organizational capacity to pursue a new conventional design. Development proceeded at the Chatham facility, but further setbacks arrived in the form of the FedCom Civil War and the Combine-Ghost Bear War, each drawing Combine resources and attention away from long-term aerospace procurement. The Oni did not complete its first flight until 3066, nearly a decade after initial planning began.

Despite the delays, the design proved worth the wait. DCMS aircrews embraced the Oni as a capable, dependable platform, and it achieved broad distribution across Combine aerospace commands. Wakazashi continued to develop the platform, producing the ON-2, which replaced the original launcher with a heavier weapon system and added an electronic warfare capability better suited to contested airspace. A separate Jihad-era experimental effort produced the ON-2X, in which Wakazashi engineers adapted stolen Capellan stealth technology acquired through the Word of Blake to create a harder-to-detect variant. Mass production of the key armor component at Chatham began in 3079, though only a single prototype existed before that threshold.

text.overview: The Ostrogoth is a 75-ton Clan heavy OmniFighter introduced by the Ghost Bear Dominion in 3078, produced at the Tseng Facility on Alshain. Designed as a direct response to mounting fighter losses during the Jihad, the Ghost Bears sought an OmniFighter that could match the agility of a medium design while carrying the armor protection of a heavier frame. The resulting aircraft exceeded the originally intended weight class, but the Dominion accepted it without hesitation, drawing on its established experience building and maintaining heavy OmniFighters. With 35 tons of configurable pod space and a reliable production base on Alshain, the Ostrogoth gave Ghost Bear aviators a versatile platform well-suited to the varied demands of late Jihad air combat.
text.capabilities:
The Ostrogoth's GM 375 extralight fusion engine delivers a Safe Thrust 7 and Maximum Thrust 11 performance profile more typical of a medium OmniFighter, despite the design's 75-ton mass. The engine's extralight configuration carries elevated maintenance costs, a trade-off the Dominion accepted in exchange for the pod space it enables. Brunin Heavy Ferro-Aluminum armor covers the airframe with 240 points of protection, providing a level of survivability closer to a true heavy fighter than the medium-weight performance envelope might suggest. Ten base double heat sinks form the standard cooling capacity, and most configurations draw additional heat sinks from their pod space allocation to manage the heat loads of energy-heavy loadouts.

The Prime configuration demonstrates the flexibility the pod space affords. A nose-mounted ER PPC and two Artemis IV-enhanced LRM-15 launchers handle long-range engagements, while a bank of six ER medium lasers delivers saturation fire at close range, with a seventh laser facing aft to discourage pursuit. A targeting computer enhances accuracy across the energy weapons, and a Guardian ECM suite degrades opponents' targeting systems. While the Ostrogoth carries less pod space than the medium designs it was meant to replace, its superior armor and comparable thrust profile make it competitive in sustained engagements where lighter fighters cannot absorb the same punishment.
text.deployment: Introduced around 3100 by the Rasalhague Dominion, the D configuration incorporates late Dark Age electronics improvements. Its nose carries an ER PPC, a Gauss rifle, and an LRM-20 with an Artemis V fire control system for improved targeting precision. A targeting computer enhances the accuracy of both the PPC and the Gauss rifle, while a Watchdog combined electronic warfare suite simultaneously disrupts enemy communications and targeting systems. The combination of precise ballistic fire, long-range energy projection, and missile volume gives D pilots broad options against opponents relying on either electronics or raw firepower. Its performance profile matches that of earlier Ostrogoth configurations, ensuring crews transitioning from other variants require minimal retraining.
text.battleHistory:
By the mid-3070s the Ghost Bear Dominion's aerospace arm was under severe strain. Heavy Jihad-era combat had taken a disproportionate toll on the Dominion's medium fighter contingent. Dependence on the aging Visigoth and the harder-to-source Jagatai had left many Stars understrength, and the lower-cost Ammon proved only a partial solution, as its performance shortfalls drove pilot casualty rates to levels the Dominion considered unacceptable. The Ghost Bears concluded that a new OmniFighter built at their own Inner Sphere manufacturing base on Alshain was the only reliable path to rebuilding their aerospace capability.

The engineering team had originally targeted a medium-weight design, but priorities around maintaining the necessary thrust profile and protecting increasingly hard-to-replace pilots pushed the mass upward. The resulting design crossed into heavy territory, but the Ghost Bears were confident in their ability to build and sustain heavy OmniFighters and approved it accordingly. The Tseng Facility on Alshain completed the first production units in 3078.

Those first Ostrogoths went directly to units staged for the Protectorate campaign. Deployed in medium Stars alongside older and slower Jengiz fighters, Ostrogoth pilots exploited the contrast in performance profiles, using their superior maneuverability to catch Blakist fighters attempting to outrun the slower designs. Blakist aviators expecting to outpace a Jengiz found themselves instead engaged by a heavy fighter matching their speed, a combination that overwhelmed the best Inner Sphere units the Word of Blake could field in the Protectorate theater.

After the Jihad, outside analysts questioned whether the cost of the Ostrogoth's large engine and supporting logistics was justified for its role when post-war militaries were reducing in size. The Dominion rejected these assessments, citing the design's proven war record and the operational economies of concentrating high capability in a single unit rather than maintaining several less capable fighters. Production continued at Alshain into the 3080s and the facility passed to the Rasalhague Dominion, which introduced a fourth alternate configuration around 3100 incorporating Dark Age-era electronics improvements.

text.overview:
The Pella is a light aerospace fighter developed by Clan Cloud Cobra during the mid-thirtieth century, named for the ancient birthplace of Alexander the Great. Designed to address a persistent threat in Homer's uninhabited lowland wastelands, the Pella was conceived as a dedicated patrol platform for locating and engaging Dark Caste elements operating beyond the reach of ground forces. Its combination of long-range sensors and standoff weapons gave Cloud Cobra aerospace commanders a self-contained tool for both reconnaissance and direct action against bandit camps and fleeing raiders.

The Pella never entered sustained production and remains one of the more tragic footnotes in Cloud Cobra aerospace history. A catastrophic incident at the fighter's public debut in 2954 tied the design to scandal at the highest levels of Clan leadership, and the project was cancelled before the aircraft could prove its operational worth. The Pella's brief existence stands as a reminder of how quickly inter-Clan rivalry can destroy a promising design program.
text.capabilities:
The Pella is built around a 280 XL Fusion engine mounted in the Type 403-21J airframe, providing strong thrust for a forty-ton platform while keeping structural mass to a minimum. Forging II Ferro-Aluminum armor protects the fuselage, offering competitive survivability for the weight class without significantly burdening the power plant. The centerpiece of the design's mission package is an integrated Beagle active probe, allowing pilots to sweep wide areas for concealed machinery and hidden 'Mechs without closing to visual range, a capability specifically tailored to the patrol conditions on Homer.

In combat, the Pella's primary weapons are two Series XIV Extended-Range Large Lasers, positioned to engage targets well beyond the effective range of most opponents in its weight class. This standoff capability directly supports the design's bandit-hunting mission, allowing pilots to engage flushed Dark Caste raiders from a distance that limits return fire options. A single Type OVR-X LB 5-X Autocannon provides supplementary burst-fire capability for shorter-range engagements, and the combined loadout performs adequately in air superiority roles against similarly-massed craft.

The design carries notable trade-offs. The emphasis on extended-range weapons creates heat management demands on prolonged patrols, and the lack of close-in defensive armament leaves the Pella exposed if a target closes to knife-fight range. The CCC T-55 communications system and CCC D5.2J targeting and tracking system reflect Cloud Cobra's in-house electronics production, providing reliable coverage suited to Homer's operating environment.
text.deployment: The Pella was produced only in limited prototype numbers, with no confirmed operational service outside the three airframes employed during the 2954 Kardaan Airfield demonstration. A small production run was subsequently completed by Clan Coyote after their acquisition of the project data, but these aircraft were captured in the 2957 Trial of Possession and ordered dismantled by Khan McCloud. No surviving examples are known to exist, and the Pella was never distributed to any other Clan or integrated into standard aerospace wing tables of organization. The Complex H-3 production facility on Homer, the sole manufacturing site for the design, was converted to OmniFighter production following the end of the program.
text.battleHistory:
Clan Cloud Cobra commissioned the Pella in the early 2950s as part of an ongoing effort to suppress the Dark Caste activity plaguing Homer's vast lowland wastes. Scavengers had long used the uninhabited territory beyond the Cloud Cobra enclaves as staging grounds, stripping salvage from downed equipment and launching raids on outlying facilities. Existing aerospace assets were too generalized for the precision tracking the mission required, and the Cobra leadership directed Complex H-3 on Homer to develop a dedicated counter-Caste platform. The resulting design, named for the Macedonian birthplace of Alexander the Great, was built around an active sensor suite paired with long-range weapons, giving pilots the ability to locate and engage targets without closing to engagement range.

The Pella's public debut on 10 September 2954 at Kardaan Memorial Airfield on Homer was intended as a formal demonstration before Khan Patrick McCloud, with delegations from Clans Sea Fox and Snow Raven in attendance. Star Colonel Samson Izumi, who had contributed to the fighter's specifications, commanded the exhibition. The event turned catastrophic when one pilot suddenly lost control and put his aircraft on a collision course with the Khan's observation platform. Izumi and his remaining pilots were forced to shoot down the errant Pella to protect McCloud's life. Investigation of the incident later revealed that Clan Coyote operatives had tampered with the prototype in advance of their planned invasion of Cloud Cobra territory on Homer, hoping the confusion would mask their offensive. Though the attempt on McCloud's life failed, his association with the incident was enough for him to end the project entirely.

The three remaining Pella prototypes were still airborne when a Coyote force arrived over the airfield, invading without declaring a formal batchall. Izumi's pilots engaged the aggressors immediately, downing two Coyote fighters before losing two of their own Pellas and forcing the third into a crash landing. In the aftermath, the Coyotes acquired the Pella's project data through undisclosed means and pressed a small production run into service as a calculated insult against the Cloud Cobras. When Khan McCloud learned of this, he declared a formal batchall over the Homer production facility in 2957. Star Colonel Izumi won the bidding with the 214th Cobra Fangs and led a Trial of Possession that devolved into a free-for-all across the Coyote's main Homer enclave after several downed fighters crashed into civilian-caste areas. Izumi claimed isorla over all Pellas the Coyotes had produced, McCloud ordered them dismantled for parts, and the Complex H-3 facility was repurposed for OmniFighter manufacturing, ending the Pella's service life entirely.

text.overview: The Picaroon stands as the Regulan Fiefs' first domestically produced aerospace fighter, a milestone reflecting the sub-state's ambition to build an indigenous defense industry following the collapse of the Free Worlds League. Designed and manufactured by Gutierrez Aerospace at their Ellsworth facility, the fighter entered service in 3097 as an apparent response to the growing use of pocket WarShips among neighboring powers. Gutierrez built the Picaroon as a purpose-built anti-shipping platform, concentrating the design's resources into speed, heavy protection, and a single devastating weapon, drawing immediate comparisons to earlier ship-killing designs like the Hammerhead. The resulting fighter achieves its greatest effectiveness when operating as part of a disciplined flight group, concentrating firepower to bring down targets that no individual fighter could threaten alone.
text.capabilities:
The Picaroon is built around a single offensive system, a nose-mounted Magna Supernova heavy particle projection cannon that concentrates the fighter's entire combat output into one weapon capable of destroying most opponents in only a few bursts. Powered by a Magna 210 extralight fusion engine, the fighter achieves a level of speed notable for a design carrying 12.5 tons of Durallex Aviator ferro-aluminum protection, giving it a defensive profile that substantially exceeds most comparably massed light fighters. The P Standard frame underlying the design is straightforward and well-understood, contributing to the fighter's Easy to Maintain rating and supporting sustained operations without specialized parts or technical expertise.

The single-weapon configuration creates an inherent vulnerability that experienced opponents exploit. Because individual Picaroons depend entirely on one cannon, smart enemies work to isolate them from their flight groups, bringing multiple attackers to bear and neutralizing the armor advantage through concentrated fire. The tendency of the heavy armor to inspire overconfidence in pilots compounds this tactical exposure, making formation discipline more critical for Picaroon effectiveness than for most comparable designs. The Picaroon achieves its best results when pilots maintain pack cohesion and coordinate fire against targets far beyond what any single fighter could engage alone.

The design carries the Atmospheric Flight Instability quirk, imposing handling challenges in planetary atmospheres that require experienced pilots to manage. This characteristic reinforces the premium the Picaroon places on skilled, disciplined crews.
text.deployment: The CSR-F100 serves as the standard aerospace fighter of the Regulan Fiefs throughout the Dark Age, equipping Regulan Hussar commands and the mercenary companies contracted for Fiefs defense. Following the reformation of the Free Worlds League, the Ellsworth facility continued production under the reconstituted League, maintaining the CSR-F100 as the sole production variant. Outside its home state, the design appears in the inventories of Duchy of Tamarind-Abbey forces and numerous mercenary commands operating throughout former Free Worlds League space, making the CSR-F100 a recognizable fixture across the region despite its relatively modest production numbers.
text.battleHistory:
The Picaroon took shape during the political fragmentation that followed the Jihad's devastation of the Free Worlds League. As the League dissolved into successor states, Gutierrez Aerospace found its output increasingly directed toward the Regulan Fiefs rather than the broader League defense establishment. The Fiefs, seeking to establish an independent defense industry, commissioned the Picaroon project as a purpose-built domestic platform, and Gutierrez introduced the design from their Ellsworth facility in 3097.

The fighter saw active combat almost immediately. During the Victoria War, Picaroon-equipped formations from the Kraken Unleashed mercenary command defended the world of Fronde against the First Andurien Cavalry, using their speed and heavy armor to make sweeping attacks against Andurien DropShips. The tenacious Andurien Cavalry fighters proved unable to prevent the Kraken Picaroons from destroying their transports, forcing the invasion force to abandon its conventional complement before reaching orbit.

The 3115 engagement over Finsterwalde, which became known as the Finsterwalde Folly, illustrated both the Picaroon's pack-hunting capability and the overconfidence problem that would shadow the design throughout its service history. A Duchy of Tamarind-Abbey Picaroon flight and a Flying Tomkats mercenary flight each launched simultaneous attacks on the other's DropShips, ignoring each other to pursue their respective targets. Both sides succeeded in destroying the enemy transports, but both also found themselves stranded in deep space without a way home. The engagement became a cautionary example often cited in discussions of the Picaroon's tendency to breed recklessness, a reputation the design never fully shed.

Despite being developed for the Regulan Fiefs, the Picaroon gradually spread to other buyers, appearing in Duchy of Tamarind-Abbey inventories and various mercenary commands, reflecting Gutierrez's willingness to sell beyond Regulan political borders and the fighter's growing combat reputation across the former League's fragmented successor states.

text.deployment: The L3 trades the Y3's mixed armament entirely for a pair of extended-range large lasers supplemented by additional heat sinking, optimized for engagements at distances where the primary model's medium-range weapons are ineffective. The L3 is best suited to pilots who prefer to engage at extended range, where it can threaten heavier fighters and suppress DropShip point defense before a main engagement. It performs poorly in close-range maneuvering fights where the Y3 is more capable.

The R3 was developed with two complementary roles in mind. Its all-pulse-laser armament emphasizes saturation fire suitable for strafing conventional infantry formations and vehicle concentrations, where the high rate of shots compensates for reduced individual weapon power. In space operations, its dense short-range fire pattern suits it to missile defense escort duties, a role that has grown in relevance as Q-ships increasingly operate in lieu of dedicated WarShips across the former Free Worlds League sphere. The R3's firepower profile makes it a poor choice for peer-fighter engagements, but it fills its specialized roles with a level of efficiency that the more general Y3 cannot match.

The A configuration reflects Nova Cat experience operating in the contested airspace of the Clan Invasion, with a loadout emphasizing close-range firepower for the dogfights that characterized Operation REVIVAL air operations. A-configuration Qasars flew in support of advancing Nova Cat ground forces as they secured the Irece District, engaging Draconis Combine aerospace assets over the occupied worlds and providing cover for DropShip operations.

The B configuration trades some short-range punch for improved mid-range output, suiting the Qasar's speed advantages in engagements where distance can be managed by the faster fighter. It was fielded by Nova Cat warriors seeking to extend their effective engagement range while retaining the agility that made the Qasar valuable, and was particularly favored in patrol and reconnaissance escort roles where an engagement might need to be broken off before fuel reserves ran low.

A late Clan Invasion era variant, the D configuration incorporates refinements drawn from Nova Cat operational experience in the Inner Sphere. Deployed in the Irece District alongside the C and A configurations, it represented the Nova Cat effort to extract maximum utility from an aging design against an increasingly capable opponent. D-configuration Qasars were still in service when the revolt began in 3141, flying in the engagements against Combine garrison forces that briefly reasserted Nova Cat control of Irece's airspace.

The base configuration introduced with the original design, the Prime carries a weapons load emphasizing long-range Clan energy weapons and missiles to exploit the Qasar's superior thrust in opening engagements. Nova Cat aerospace warriors preferred it for Trials of Position and honor duels where speed could be used to dictate engagement range. The Prime served as the reference configuration throughout the Qasar's active service life with Clan Nova Cat and formed the basis from which later variants were developed.

The RPR-100b was produced exclusively for SLDF Royal units during the Star League era, representing an enhanced version of the standard Rapier reserved for elite formations. It never reached the broader Lyran market during active production. Like most Royal variants, the RPR-100b became extremely rare during the First Succession War as the Royal Brigades were scattered and destroyed across multiple campaigns. Surviving examples became valued prizes for salvagers, collectors, and deep-periphery factions. No resumed production of the type is known to have occurred after the fall of the Star League.

The RPR-100b-EC is a field refit associated with Clan Wolverine forces during their exodus and subsequent operations following the Pentagon Civil War. Technical records of the modification are fragmentary at best, as the Wolverines' eventual annihilation by combined Clan forces destroyed most documentation of the program. Surviving assessments suggest the refit adapted the Royal 100b's advanced equipment to accommodate the constraints of sustained deep-space operations far from Inner Sphere supply infrastructure. No examples are believed to remain in operational condition, and the type is classified as extinct for practical purposes.

The RPR-200 was built exclusively for the SLDF's Royal Regiments, representing the most capable variant of the Star League-era Rapier family. Armed with extended-range particle cannons and a high-capacity autocannon in place of the standard loadout, and protected by heavy ferro-aluminum armor well above the base model's specification, the RPR-200 was a substantially more dangerous craft than any contemporary Rapier variant. Its combat service was limited to the elite formations of the Royal Brigades and, reportedly, a small number of examples were carried into the Exodus with Kerensky's forces. No RPR-200 airframes are believed to remain in operational condition in the Inner Sphere, and technical documentation adequate to reconstruct the variant's advanced systems is considered lost.

The RPR-300 entered service as a product of the Word of Blake's Tharkad occupation, produced at the captured Lockheed/CBM facilities as a comprehensively redesigned version bearing the Rapier name. The Blakist configuration replaced the original's ballistic and missile-heavy armament with a focused energy weapons array optimized for sustained engagements at range, making it a capable multi-role fighter by Jihad-era standards. When Lyran forces retook Tharkad, they recognized the military value of the existing production line immediately and continued RPR-300 manufacturing even while Lockheed/CBM engineers developed the follow-on RPR-300S. The RPR-300 remains in frontline Lyran service alongside its successor, and the two variants are frequently deployed together in mixed lances that exploit their nearly identical performance envelopes.
text.battleHistory:
Bauer Enterprises had built its reputation on consumer electronics before the Rapier changed everything. When the company announced plans to enter the military aerospace market in 2590, established contractors were politely skeptical. The SLDF took a different view. With the Reunification War still grinding forward and procurement officers under constant pressure to expand the League's fighter inventory, any viable proposal deserved consideration. Bauer's design had serious problems, the simultaneous-firing configuration of its twin particle cannons caused a cooling cascade that killed a test pilot during development and forced months of redesign before the cockpit life support system met safety standards; but the end result was a craft the SLDF wanted enough to wait for. Production began in 2596, and the Rapier quickly established itself as a capable heavy striker for the League's fighter lances.

The design's association with the Lyran Commonwealth developed early and became permanent. The Tharkad-based factory gave House Steiner natural access to newly produced frames, and Lyran aerospace forces received substantial deliveries alongside SLDF formations throughout the Star League era. When the League fell, it was the Lyran military that inherited the largest share of surviving production capacity and in-service airframes. The Rapier would carry that Lyran identity for generations.

The Star League's collapse was not immediately catastrophic for Bauer Enterprises. The factory on Tharkad survived the opening decades of the Succession Wars largely intact - never directly attacked, though operating under increasingly difficult conditions. What the wars destroyed was not the physical plant but the supply network that fed it. The advanced targeting system at the heart of the Rapier's capabilities required components and manufacturing tolerances that became unavailable as interstellar trade collapsed. By the early Second Succession War, Bauer could no longer produce the full-specification Rapier. The factory quietly shifted to the simplified RPR-102 configuration, replacing precision particle cannon assemblies with large lasers and adding conventional heat sinks to compensate. Even in this reduced form the Rapier remained a fixture in Lyran and later FedCom inventories through the Renaissance period, and intercepted intelligence during the late Civil War era hinted that Bauer was quietly exploring a full-specification revival.

The Jihad ended that prospect violently. The Word of Blake's assault on Tharkad in late 3067 and early 3068 destroyed the Bauer Enterprises facility outright, eliminating the original production line and most of its institutional knowledge. The Word then turned to Tharkad's other major aerospace manufacturer, Lockheed/CBM Corporation, which had survived the initial assault. Using line equipment and technical documentation captured during the occupation, Blakist engineers rebuilt the Rapier from the ground up. The RPR-300 series that entered service in 3074 bore the Rapier's name and general configuration but replaced the old ballistic and missile-heavy loadout with a focused energy weapons array built around the captured Lockheed/CBM production infrastructure.

When Lyran forces finally retook Tharkad and secured the Lockheed/CBM facilities, they inherited both the production line and a complicated political problem. The RPR-300 was capable enough that scrapping it would have been tactically foolish, but its Blakist origins made it deeply unpopular in a Commonwealth that had paid dearly for the Jihad. Lockheed/CBM's answer was the RPR-300S, which made modest but real improvements to the weapons layout and allowed the design to be relaunched under a new Steiner designation. Critics noted that the 300S and its predecessor were functionally very similar (enemy aerospace pilots were known to have difficulty distinguishing them in combat) but the Commonwealth procurement establishment accepted the rebadging as politically necessary. The 300S entered service in 3081 and became the standard production Rapier for the modern Lyran aerospace force, deployed widely across frontline and garrison formations alike.

Throughout this long history, every variant of the Rapier traces its origins to Tharkad. From Bauer Enterprises' original gamble in 2590 to the Lockheed/CBM production lines of the ilClan era, the fighter has remained what it always was: a Tharkad product and a Lyran institution.

text.overview: The Raubvogel--roughly translated as "bird of prey" in the archaic German favored by Lyran military tradition--is one of the most widely deployed conventional bomber designs in Lyran service. Produced by Lockheed/CBM Corporation, the AB-18 series has gone through numerous iterations since its initial introduction, with the AB-18C variant representing the current standard configuration as of 3064. The forty-five-ton ICE-powered design fills the atmospheric close support role that heavier aerospace fighters are often considered too valuable to perform, providing ground commanders with responsive and affordable fire support at a fraction of the cost of committing a dedicated strike aerospace fighter to the same mission.
text.capabilities:
The AB-18C mounts a nose-mounted large laser as its primary weapon, backed by a nose-mounted SRM 2 and a pair of wing-mounted Streak SRM 4 launchers. The large laser provides reliable strafing capability against armored targets without ammunition constraints, while the Streak missile systems ensure that every launched missile finds its mark--a critical efficiency for a bomber that must make the most of each attack pass. The ICE powerplant limits the fighter's speed to a safe thrust of four, making it slower than most competitors but adequate for ground-attack profiles.

Armor protection is distributed across all facings with emphasis on the nose and wings, reflecting the fighter's expected approach angles during bombing runs. Eight heat sinks manage the thermal load from the large laser. External hardpoints are the Raubvogel's greatest tactical asset--commanders commonly fit the AB-18C with an external TAG unit and four one-ton laser-guided bombs for precision close support missions, transforming the bomber into a highly effective designator-striker platform.
text.deployment: The Raubvogel is ubiquitous in the Lyran Alliance and has spread extensively into the Federated Suns through the legacy of the Federated Commonwealth. Planetary militias, garrison commands, and even some frontline regiments employ the AB-18C for atmospheric ground support duties that do not warrant committing aerospace fighters. The bomber's straightforward maintenance requirements and use of widely available components make it a favorite of logisticians on budget-constrained garrison worlds.
text.battleHistory:
Lockheed/CBM Corporation has produced the AB-18 series for decades, iterating through multiple variants as available technology advanced and new weapons systems entered widespread production. The AB-18C emerged during the early 3060s as Lockheed/CBM integrated Streak missile technology into the proven airframe, replacing earlier conventional SRM systems that wasted ammunition on near-misses during the high-speed attack runs typical of bomber operations. The improved hit rate more than justified the increased cost per missile for budget-conscious garrison commands.

The Federated Commonwealth era proved enormously beneficial for the Raubvogel's market reach. Lyran production facilities supplied the design to both halves of the combined state, establishing maintenance infrastructure and spare parts networks across the Federated Suns. Even after the FedCom Civil War fragmented those supply chains, the bomber's established logistics footprint ensured it remained in widespread Davion service. The Raubvogel's remarkable longevity is proof of Lockheed/CBM's philosophy of incremental improvement rather than radical redesign--each new variant built on the proven reliability of its predecessor while incorporating the latest field-tested technologies.

text.deployment: The F-700a's combination of an LB 10-X autocannon and eight SRM-6 racks made it the preferred close-range Riever variant for pilots who favored sustained missile volume over ammunition conservation. Three production facilities served the type: Andurien, Westover, and an additional Lopez factory that operated through the Jihad period before ceasing output. The variant's adoption across Free Worlds League, Star League, Word of Blake, and Federated Suns forces made it one of the most widely distributed Riever configurations in service during the thirty-first and thirty-second centuries. The Andurien factory continued production under Duchy of Andurien ownership through the Dark Age and into the ilClan era, and the Westover line remained active under independent and later Rim Commonality ownership before returning to League hands.

production.manufacturer: Andurien AeroTech (A Division of Free Worlds Defense Industries)|Andurien AeroTech (A Division of Free Worlds Defense Industries)|Andurien AeroTech (A Division of Free Worlds Defense Industries)|Kurita Combine Munitions Corporation

text.deployment: The F-700b entered service during the FedCom Civil War period, produced at Andurien and Westover under Free Worlds League oversight. A separate Word of Blake production contract at the Altair facility added a Jihad-era supply of the variant, though that line ceased operations when League forces reclaimed the world post-Jihad. The Andurien plant resumed production under Duchy of Andurien control and built the variant continuously through the Dark Age and into the ilClan era. The Westover facility's output was interrupted during the Jihad but eventually resumed under independent ownership, then passed through Rim Commonality hands before returning to League control. The F-700b's upgraded armor and enhanced weapons suite made it the preferred Riever for front-line combat assignments throughout the thirty-second century.

Deployed exclusively with SLDF Royal command formations, the Eb variant incorporated advanced technology that set it apart from standard production Rogues. An XL engine replaced the conventional power plant, freeing mass that was invested in upgraded laser weapons and Artemis IV fire control for the LRM launchers. Double heat sinks completed the package. The Eb represented the pinnacle of Rogue development, but its restriction to Royal units meant very few were ever produced, and virtually all examples were lost during the Amaris Crisis and the Exodus that followed. Those that survived are counted among the rarest Star League-era aerospace designs still in the Inner Sphere.

The F variant was developed as a ground-attack platform during the early Star League era. Replacing each wing-mounted LRM-15 with a pair of short-range missile launchers gave the craft heavier close-in punch suitable for supporting operations against BattleMechs and armored vehicles, and the airframe was modified to carry bombs for area bombardment. The variant's poor handling limited its effectiveness against enemy fighters, and it was typically assigned to missions where air defense suppression had already been established or ground targets were the primary objective.

The L variant exchanged the original missile systems for a pair of large lasers, producing a strafing configuration suited to sustained fire against ground targets. Six additional heat sinks were added to manage the increased energy load. Introduced during the late Star League era and adopted by Lyran Commonwealth forces, the variant's energy armament freed it from dependence on ammunition resupply, making it useful for extended patrol or operations where supply lines were uncertain. Surviving L-model airframes remained in Lyran service until the factory's destruction ended new production.

Developed by the Com Guards as an upgrade of surviving L-model airframes in the 3050s, the LP variant replaced standard heat sinks with double heat sinks and upgraded the laser suite to pulse laser versions, substantially improving both accuracy and heat management. The result was one of the most potent configurations the airframe had ever carried and became a favorite among Com Guard aerospace pilots. Despite its performance, the LP remained rare, accounting for only about ten percent of ComStar's active Rogue inventory. It saw action through the Jihad and remained in service into the Dark Age with Com Guard and Word of Blake units.

A Lyran Commonwealth field refit introduced during the Second Succession War, the P variant replaced the missile systems with a pair of particle projection cannons and added two additional heat sinks. The configuration offered a significant increase in raw hitting power, but the thermal demands of firing both weapons simultaneously proved difficult to manage with the Rogue's limited heat dissipation, and pilots frequently lost control of their aircraft when attempting maximum fire output. The variant saw use along the Lyran border with the Free Worlds League, where its range and damage potential were valued even if its reliability was not.

text.deployment: The SB-27 became one of the most widely deployed light aerospace fighters in Inner Sphere history through Raimei's production network, appearing in planetary garrison forces across all five Great Houses, the Magistracy of Canopus, and the Taurian Concordat. Following Raimei's financial collapse, surviving production lines at Jalastar Aerospace, Lockheed/CBM, Majesty Metals and Manufacturing, and Pinard Protectorates Limited continued supplying their respective factions' garrison commands. The design remains active at Jalastar on Panpour and Pinard on Organo as a standard low-cost garrison platform through the ilClan era.

text.deployment: The SB-27b was produced for SLDF Royal units during the Amaris Civil War and saw service in the campaign to liberate Terra. Production was limited to Star League-era facilities operating the Royal upgrade package. Following Kerensky's Exodus, SB-27b airframes dispersed into the militaries of the Pentagon states and their successors, though active production ceased with the collapse of the Star League manufacturing network. Jalastar Aerospace restarted production of the SB-27b on Panpour in the Dark Age era using the New Dallas Memory Core data.

The SB-27b-EC was exclusive to Clan Cloud Cobra during the Pentagon Campaign, where Cobra technicians modified the Clan's surviving SB-27b Royal airframes with four prototype extended-range lasers. The variant never entered formal production and serves as a field-modified interim configuration, bridging the end of the Inner Sphere Royal program and the Clans' early access to advanced extended-range weapon technology. All surviving examples remained in Cloud Cobra inventory.

The SB-28 was originally produced in limited quantities exclusively for the Terran Hegemony Navy at the Raimei/Lockheed facility on Outreach beginning in 2753, and was not shared with other factions at that time. The variant went dormant following the Star League's collapse. During the Jihad, Lockheed/CBM produced the SB-28 on Donegal for the Kell Hounds and Federated Suns forces until that facility was destroyed in 3072. Jalastar Aerospace on Panpour resumed production in 3074 using specifications supplied by Clan Wolf-in-Exile through the Kell Hounds, and continues to produce the SB-28 for Federated Suns and mercenary customers.

Wakazashi's first Sabre-family production for the Draconis Combine since the collapse of the Raimei network, the SB-29 serves as a standard light garrison and patrol fighter in DCMS and Draconis Combine Admiralty inventories. The type appears widely across DC system garrisons and aboard DCA support vessels, restoring the Sabre name to active Combine aerospace assets after decades of absence from Combine production lines.

The Defense Special was never formally offered for sale or officially acknowledged as a production unit. Wakazashi's procurement offices persistently denied knowledge of its existence, and no confirmed deployments to DCMS or DCA operational forces have been recorded. Its existence came to light through ComStar Strategic Developments analysis rather than any public documentation. The fighter remains a prototype series whose operational use, if any, has not been substantiated. Full production was eventually shifted to the improved SB-31D variant.

The SB-31D was offered to the Draconis Combine Admiralty in 3079 for deployment as close escort for WarShips, DropShips, and JumpShips. The DCA credits the type with intercepting or stopping several Blakist missile salvos during the Jihad, though material verification of these claims has not been made available. The fighter is rarely used in offensive missions and functions as a defensive specialist, deployed in lance or larger formations screening Combine capital assets. Wakazashi also maintains SB-31Ds for its own corporate shipping protection at Kervil.

The A configuration is a dedicated close-range strike loadout, concentrating three heavy autocannons for maximum burst damage on a single pass. The extreme firepower comes at the cost of limited ammunition, restricting the A to short-duration high-intensity engagements rather than prolonged patrol duties. Backup energy weapons provide minimal coverage during withdrawal, but the A's primary value lies in its ability to rapidly overwhelm heavily armored targets before disengaging to rearm. It is most effective against DropShips and capital aerospace where its massed fire can quickly strip defensive plating.

The C configuration is the Sabutai's pure energy specialist, mounting ER large and medium lasers with no reliance on ammunition. Additional heat sink capacity integrated into the pod loadout manages the thermal demands of sustained fire, making it one of the few Sabutai variants capable of extended independent operations. The C excels at strafing runs against ground targets and protracted dogfights where resupply is unavailable, combining good reach with solid damage output across multiple arcs.

The D configuration builds on the C's all-energy philosophy, replacing its long-reach lasers with heavy large lasers for greater damage at shorter engagement distances. Extended heat sink capacity manages the increased thermal burden, though even so the D must manage its fire rate carefully in sustained combat. The configuration is most effective at close engagement distances, making it a preferred choice for pilots who prefer aggressive tactics and forcing a merge with the enemy.

The Prime configuration leads with a nose-mounted Gauss rifle, providing precise long-range engagement capability with minimal heat penalty. Wing-mounted ER PPCs and large pulse lasers deliver powerful follow-through at intermediate ranges, while a pair of rear-arc small lasers discourage pursuit. The combination makes the Prime a balanced all-aspect performer suited to fleet engagements and DropShip escort duty alike, and it has seen wide distribution across nearly every Clan that has fielded the Sabutai.

The thirty S-3 prototypes served exclusively with the Draconis Combine Military Service, deployed on raids against Federated Commonwealth space during the late Succession Wars. These engagements validated the Sai concept against contemporary Davion and Steiner fighter designs. The S-3 effectively gave way to the S-4X on the production line before Schuyler could build meaningful numbers, leaving the original variant as a limited-run design found in small numbers with frontline Combine units that participated in the field evaluation program.

Entering service in 3061 following the recapture of Schuyler from Clan Smoke Jaguar, the S-4 replaced the original laser armament with an ER PPC and Artemis IV-enhanced SRM launchers, giving Combine pilots a more capable weapons package across multiple engagement ranges. It became the standard production variant from Schuyler through the Jihad and into the Dark Age, serving as the primary light fighter of Combine wings throughout the Civil War era and the early thirty-second century.

Produced by Clan Smoke Jaguar at the occupied Schuyler facility following the Clan Invasion, the S-4C was deployed to several second-line clusters during the occupation. After Operation Bulldog, Wakazashi engineers could not replicate the Clan-tech production process. Later Dark Age production at the Avon facility (a Combine and Nova Cat cooperative venture) and refit operations at the Barcella Delta center on Irece extended the S-4C's service life well into the thirty-second century, making it a continuing presence in Combine light fighter inventories.

The S-4X entered production at Schuyler in 3048 as a demonstration of recovered Star League technology applied to the Sai airframe, earning distinction as the first Inner Sphere fighter of the thirty-first century to mount an extralight fusion engine. Production was cut short by the Smoke Jaguar capture of Schuyler in 3050, leaving only a small number of completed examples. Those few S-4X fighters were highly regarded by their pilots for their significant improvements in firepower and protection relative to the base S-3.

Developed during the Civil War era and entering service in 3065, the S-7 reorients the Sai toward long-range patrol and escort, trading the ER PPC for dual ER medium lasers and replacing the wing missile bays with MRM launchers. An increased fuel load extends operational range, making it well-suited for deployment on border worlds where patrol endurance matters. The S-7 filled a recognized gap in the Combine's light fighter inventory and has been widely distributed to DCMS units along the Combine's frontiers.

Introduced just prior to the Jihad in 3069, the S-8 carries an all-energy weapons suite combining light PPCs in the nose with ER medium lasers in each wing, eliminating all ammunition dependence and simplifying logistics in sustained campaign conditions. The upgrade to ferro-aluminum armor improves survivability. The S-8 proved its value throughout the Jihad period and continues to serve in Combine inventories through the Dark Age, representing the most recent conventional production evolution of the Sai line.

The SL-25 served as the Terran Hegemony's primary ground attack fighter through the Age of War and much of the Star League era, distributed to SLDF and member-state units engaged in sustained planetary operations. After the Amaris Coup ended production on Mizar, surviving examples filtered into Lyran and other successor-state inventories, where they continued in service with progressively scarcer spare parts. By the late Succession Wars period the highest concentrations were found in the Outworlds Alliance, a distribution shaped by the Samurai's earlier history of operations against that nation's forces.

The SL-26 was produced in limited numbers for SLDF units during the Star League era and was not widely distributed outside that force. Its advanced technologies placed it beyond the production capabilities of most member-state facilities, and the type did not spread significantly into successor-state inventories before the Second Succession War eliminated the last surviving examples. No SL-26 is known to have survived that conflict.

The SL-27 entered production during the Jihad through the rebuilt Fairchild Dornier facility on Mizar, with Lyran Alliance and ComStar subsidies underwriting the restart. Lyran interest was driven in part by shortfalls in other fighter programs, making the revived Samurai line a practical alternative for units in need of proven ground attack capability. Limited production kept distribution tight, and the SL-27 did not reach the numbers necessary to become a common type in any major aerospace force.

The primary Schrack configuration fills the interceptor and anti-DropShip roles for Republic aerospace wings. Its improved heavy Gauss rifle provides the range and penetrating power needed to threaten large, slow-moving targets, while nose-mounted ER medium lasers and wing-mounted Streak launchers give the pilot effective close-range coverage during sustained engagements. The primary configuration is most commonly assigned to fleet escort and high-priority intercept missions, and serves as the standard Republic loadout where flexibility and anti-DropShip capability are equally important.

The A configuration trades the primary's improved heavy Gauss rifle for a conventional Gauss rifle and redirects significant pod weight toward a dense array of ER medium lasers spread across both wings and the aft arc, with six additional double heat sinks to support the heavier energy weapon load. This arrangement provides broader coverage across multiple firing arcs and is favored for engagements where sustained medium-range pressure matters more than long-range anti-armor capability. The A configuration shares the interceptor role with the primary and is most commonly deployed alongside SCK-O variants in mixed squadrons, where complementary loadouts cover different threat profiles.

The A configuration adapts the Scytha to a missile-intensive role, sustaining bombardment across multiple range bands with paired long-range launchers on each wing. A Narc missile beacon in the nose improves targeting data for allied units, making the A configuration valuable in coordinated aerospace operations. Limited ammunition reserves require access to rearming facilities in sustained campaigns, restricting its use to operations with reliable logistics support.

text.deployment: The C configuration prioritizes long-range engagements, relying on Gauss rifles and extended-range particle cannons to engage targets before they close to optimal range. Twin medium pulse lasers provide a close-in backup. The Gauss reload supply limits its endurance in extended operations, but its reach allows it to establish engagement dominance early in most fighter engagements.

The D configuration returns to an autocannon-anchored approach but substitutes a Gauss rifle for cooler operation and greater range. Advanced heavy lasers and extended-range lasers on each wing extend the damage envelope, and additional heat sinks allow sustained fire across multiple passes. The Gauss reload supply remains the primary constraint on operational duration.

The F configuration is a Dark Age loadout designed for close-range dominance, combining improved heavy large lasers with a large autocannon and Streak missiles. A Watchdog combined electronics warfare suite adds countermeasure and sensor disruption capability. A targeting computer ties together the autocannon and laser array. Documented primarily in Jade Falcon aerospace units during the post-Jihad period.

The primary configuration of the Scytha and the most widely fielded across Jade Falcon aerospace wings. Its combination of heavy autocannon firepower and laser coverage makes it a capable strike platform against both opposing fighters and ground targets. Paired aft weapons provide genuine deterrence against pursuit. The limited autocannon ammunition supply encourages disciplined fire discipline, and pilots typically reserve high-volume bursts for decisive passes.

A unique single-unit field modification, this Seydlitz replaces the standard fusion engine with an XL model, using the weight savings to add an extra ton of internal fuel and increase total armor protection to three and a half tons. The standard large laser is swapped for a snub-nose PPC, providing an alternative energy weapon with no minimum engagement range at the cost of shorter maximum reach. No factory production exists for this configuration; it is a one-off custom modification documented in Record Sheets: Unique Fighters.

The original production Seydlitz entered service in 2504 as the standard Lyran Commonwealth light interceptor, deployed primarily on small border worlds and in DropShip escort squadrons where speed and energy weapons made maintenance manageable for garrison commands. The fighter's limitations in armor and fuel were well understood, and Lyran doctrine developed around coordinated squadron strikes rather than individual engagements. Paired with heavier fighters such as the Chippewa or supported by ground-based assets, the SYD-21 proved highly effective as a screening and harassment platform throughout the Succession Wars. The model continued in front-line service well into the thirty-first century and remained in production at Taurus Territorial Industries on Sterope and the United Outworlders Corporation on Ramora in addition to the primary Shipil line on Skye.
